raw_segments.text: When the duke occupied the Rah Magna, he found it under the rule of weak masters, who rather
plundered their subjects than ruled them, and gave them more cause for disunion than
for union, so that the country was full of robbery, quarrels, and every kind of violence.

Thereupon he promoted Messer-Ramiro-Dorco, a swift and cruel man, to whom he gave the
This man, in a short time, restored peace and unity with the greatest success.
Afterwards the duke considered that it was not advisable to confer such excessive authority,
for he had no doubt but that he would become odious, so he set up a court of judgment in
the country, under a most excellent president, wherein all cities had their advocates.
And because he knew that the past severity had caused some hatred against himself, so,
to clear himself in the minds of the people, and gain them entirely to himself, he desired
to show that, if any cruelty had been practiced, it had not originated with him, but in the
Under this pretense he took Rah-Miro, and one morning caused him to be executed and
left on the piazza at Sesina with the block and a bloody knife at his side.
The barbarity of this spectacle caused the people to be at once satisfied and dismayed.
